The Cook Political Report's Partisan Voting Index (PVI) is a measure of how strongly a congressional district leans towards either the Democratic or Republican party. It is calculated by comparing a district's vote in the past two presidential elections to the national average. The PVI is displayed as a letter (D or R) followed by a number, which indicates the number of percentage points above the national average that the district voted for the party indicated by the letter. In 2022, the Cook Political Report updated its formula for calculating PVI values to give more weight to the most recent presidential election.

Trans broken arm syndrome is a common form of discrimination faced by transgender individuals in healthcare settings. It occurs when a doctor mistakenly assumes that a trans person's medical ailments are related to their trans status or gender-affirming care, and as a result, treats their problem incorrectly or denies them care entirely. Trans patients often hide their trans status when seeking medical care for issues that are not related to their trans status, particularly in rural or conservative areas. A 2022 survey from the Center for American Progress found that 19% of trans individuals had experienced this form of discrimination in the past year.

Transgender people have the right to medical privacy, which is protected by the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA). This law prohibits medical providers and insurance companies from disclosing any personal medical information, including a person's transgender status, without their consent. HIPAA also gives transgender individuals the right to access and receive a copy of their medical records from healthcare facilities.

Obtaining insurance coverage for medical needs can be difficult for transgender individuals. While there is medical consensus that hormone therapy and sex reassignment surgery (SRS) are medically necessary for many transgender people, some insurance companies still do not cover these treatments. Transgender individuals may face challenges in finding insurance coverage that meets their medical needs, and may have to pay for these treatments out of pocket.
